rule_owner_words: Embed what we aren't modifying, fork what we are.
A CUI wrapper counts as modify - unless it is literally just an engine used within another process that isn't modified.
F is a files app; 9to1 Files is a files app; we extend F's features and replace its UI with CUI -> fork F.

Firefox is a browser; 9to1 Haven is a browser; we extend Firefox's features and replace its UI with CUI -> fork Firefox. Gecko is an engine used within a browser; we do not modify Gecko -> do not fork it, include it prebuilt.
Rnote has an engine and we are modifying that engine separately -> fork the engine. It is not always app=fork, engine=embed; the discriminator is what is actually being modified.
fork_policy_20261030.test: verdict follows the artifact 9to1 actually modifies, measured from patch files, our own commits and observed working-tree dirt - not from the artifact's role label. A fork scope can be narrower than the project (Rnote engine crates) or cover the application layer only (planned Firefox fork, with engine scopes kept pristine).
fork_policy_20261030.enforcement: eng/development/donor_policy.py census --repo . (read-only; exits non-zero when evidence and policy disagree, when donor trees carry unclassified changes, when a pin does not match the recorded pin, and it reports when recorded modifications are absent from the pin or a donor is a loose vendored tree)
